members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France’s objective is a technical but robust renewal of the high seas arms-embargo inspection authorization before it expires, preserving the mechanism used by Operation IRINI while supporting UNSMIL’s political road map and avoiding new obligations that could trigger a veto. The likely difficulties will be Russian and Chinese sensitivity to references to external interference, regional enforcement operations, and the balance between migration language and sovereignty; keeping the operative core close to resolution 2780 should secure at least nine votes.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling its resolution 1970 (2011) and all subsequent relevant resolutions, including resolutions 2292 (2016), 2357 (2017), 2420 (2018), 2473 (2019), 2526 (2020), 2578 (2021), 2635 (2022), 2684 (2023), 2733 (2024), 2780 (2025) and 2796 (2025),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya,

Reaffirming its resolution 2796 (2025), and stressing the importance of a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, including the full implementation of the road map announced by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on 21 August 2025,

Expressing grave concern at the continued fragile political and security situation in Libya, including armed clashes and the activities of militias and armed groups, and their impact on the stability of Libya and the region,

Expressing concern at the recent loss of life in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya and underscoring the need for comprehensive approaches to migration and refugee protection, in accordance with international law,

Reiterating its concern that the illicit proliferation of arms and related materiel in Libya continues to undermine peace, security and stability, and emphasizing the importance of full and effective implementation of the arms embargo by all Member States and all Libyan parties,

Recalling the authorizations put in place by resolution 2292 (2016), extended and amended by subsequent relevant resolutions, for the strict implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya,

Taking note of the reports of the Secretary-General on the implementation of the relevant resolutions and emphasizing the importance of continued and timely reporting,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to extend the authorizations as set out in resolution 2733 (2024), as extended by resolution 2780 (2025), for a further six months from the date of this resolution;

2. Calls upon all Member States and all Libyan parties to fully and effectively implement the arms embargo and to refrain from any actions that could undermine the political process, peace and stability of Libya;

3. Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council within five months of the adoption of this resolution on its implementation;

4. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

Algeria.change: Replace OP2 with: 'Calls upon all Member States and all Libyan parties to fully and effectively implement the arms embargo, in full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and to refrain from any actions, including external interference, that could undermine the political process, peace and stability of Libya;'
Add: 'Calls for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries from Libya without further delay, in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions;'

Replace with: 'Expressing grave concern at the recent loss of life in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya and underscoring the need for a comprehensive approach to migration and refugee protection, in accordance with international law, including by addressing root causes, saving lives and ensuring full respect for the human rights of migrants and refugees,'

China.change: Replace 'Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council within five months of the adoption of this resolution on its implementation;' with 'Requests the Secretary-General, in consultation with the Libyan authorities and relevant stakeholders, to report to the Security Council within five months of the adoption of this resolution on the implementation of this resolution, including an assessment of the effectiveness of Operation IRINI and of the handling and disposal of seized contraband, and to include recommendations for any necessary adjustment;'

Add at the end: 'Calls upon Member States implementing the authorizations to ensure that seized arms and related materiel are handled and disposed of transparently and in accordance with international law, including through timely notification and consultation with the Libyan authorities;'
Add at the end: ', and recognizing the need to take into account the views of the Libyan authorities and to adjust the authorizations in light of their effectiveness and actual needs'

Greece.change: Add a preambular paragraph: "Welcoming the continued contribution of the European Union Naval Force Mediterranean Operation IRINI to the implementation of the arms embargo, in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions;"

Strengthen the migration paragraph by adding: "and stressing the importance of countering migrant smuggling and human trafficking, including through enhanced regional cooperation and support for Libyan coast guard capacity-building in accordance with international law;"
Add after "implement the arms embargo": "through all relevant means, including by preventing illicit transfers by air, land and sea"

Guyana.change: At the end of OP1, add: ', and stresses that these authorizations shall be implemented in full accordance with international law, including the law of the sea;'

Add: 'Calls upon all Member States to ensure that implementation of the measures authorized in this resolution does not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue operations at sea, and fully respects the human rights of all persons;'

Pakistan.change: Replace with: 'Calls upon all Member States and all Libyan parties to fully and effectively implement the arms embargo while respecting Libya's sovereignty and territorial integrity, in close coordination and collaboration with the Libyan institutions and authorities concerned, and to refrain from any actions that could undermine the political process, peace and stability of Libya;'

Add: 'Directs the Sanctions Committee to take the lead on matters related to the disposal of any seized items, ensuring transparent implementation, and calls for capacity-building and training of the relevant Libyan departments to enable them to implement the arms embargo independently in the future;'

Russian Federation.change: Replace 'for a further six months from the date of this resolution' with 'for a further six months from the date of this resolution, subject to a review by the Security Council after three months on the basis of a report by the Secretary-General on the effectiveness and transparency of the inspections regime'.

Add: 'Requests the Secretary-General to include in this report a detailed assessment of the implementation of the inspections regime, including the number and outcome of inspections, any detected arms embargo violations, and the impact on legitimate maritime activity and humanitarian deliveries, and to provide recommendations for improving its effectiveness.'

Insert after 'arms embargo': 'in accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and with due regard for the sovereignty and jurisdiction of States, and without impeding legitimate trade, humanitarian deliveries, or the export of Libyan oil and gas'.

Sierra Leone.change: Replace with: 'Calls upon all Member States and all Libyan parties to fully and effectively implement the arms embargo, to refrain from any actions that could undermine the political process, peace and stability of Libya, and to cooperate fully with the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011) and the Panel of Experts, including through timely reporting on inspections, seizures and violations;'

Add: 'Decides that the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011) shall play a leading role in the disposal of prohibited arms and related materiel seized pursuant to the authorizations in paragraph 1, and requests Member States to notify the Committee of any inspection, seizure or disposal without delay;'

Replace with: 'Expressing grave concern at the recent loss of life in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya, underscoring the need for comprehensive approaches to migration and refugee protection in accordance with international law, and calling for efforts to combat smuggling and trafficking networks and to protect migrants and refugees;'

Replace with: 'Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Security Council within five months of the adoption of this resolution on its implementation, including information on inspections and seizures at sea, the disposal of prohibited arms and related materiel, and the humanitarian and migration situation;'

Slovenia.change: Add a preambular paragraph: “Reaffirming the obligation of all parties in Libya to fully respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and stressing the need to protect civilians, including migrants and refugees, and to ensure accountability for violations and abuses;”
At the end, add: “in full compliance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and relevant human rights and refugee law;”
Replace “on its implementation” with “on its implementation, including on arms embargo violations and on cooperation with the United Nations Support Mission in Libya and Operation IRINI;”

Somalia.change: Add at the end: ', and calls for enhanced coordination between relevant international actors, including Operation IRINI, and the Government of National Unity of Libya, with full respect for Libya's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity.'

Requests the Secretary-General to include in his report detailed information on the implementation of the arms embargo, including seizures and the disposal, destruction or transfer of arms and related materiel, in coordination with the 1970 Sanctions Committee, and calls for greater transparency and accountability by all Member States and relevant operations.

United States of America.change: Replace with: 'Expressing concern at the recent loss of life in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya and underscoring the need to combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking and to hold perpetrators accountable;'
Add after the road map reference: ', and stressing that UNSMIL should focus on its core political mission in line with the strategic review and establish clear performance benchmarks;'

Replace with: 'Calls upon all Member States and all Libyan parties to fully and effectively implement the arms embargo, including by preventing the illicit transfer of arms and related materiel to and from Libya, to share relevant information with the Libya Panel of Experts, and to refrain from any actions that could undermine the political process, peace and stability of Libya;'

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the arms embargo authorizations and appreciates the penholder's work. We would like the text to reinforce respect for Libya's sovereignty and non-interference and to include the longstanding call for withdrawal of foreign fighters and mercenaries, consistent with Council decisions. We also seek a stronger migration paragraph that addresses root causes and protects lives and human rights; these changes would strengthen our support and that of the A3+.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the arms embargo authorizations, but our abstentions on resolutions 2733 and 2780 reflected unresolved concerns about Operation IRINI, including transparency over seized items and the need to listen to Libya. We therefore ask the penholder to strengthen the reporting and review language and to add an explicit requirement for transparent disposal of seized contraband in consultation with the Libyan authorities. With these changes, China would be prepared to support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft as it stands and thanks France and Greece for their work as co-penholders. The renewal is essential to sustaining Operation IRINI’s implementation of the arms embargo, which remains a key tool for stabilizing Libya. We encourage swift adoption and call on all Member States and Libyan parties to fully implement the embargo and cooperate with the relevant mechanisms. We also welcome the draft’s attention to the humanitarian dimensions of migration and refugee protection in accordance with international law.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports a clean six-month renewal and thanks France for the draft. As co-penholder, we would like the text to reflect the Council’s continued recognition of Operation IRINI’s role in implementing the arms embargo and to strengthen the migration and trafficking language given the recent tragedies off the Libyan coast. We can be flexible on placement, but we should preserve the existing authorizations intact and reinforce implementation by air, land and sea.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the high-seas authorizations and welcomes the draft's references to the Libyan-led political process and the loss of life in the Mediterranean. We request a minor amendment to OP1 to make explicit that implementation is in full accordance with international law, including the law of the sea, and a new OP after OP2 to include a humanitarian and search-and-rescue safeguard. These clarifications would strengthen the legal and humanitarian basis of the mandate without altering its scope.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the technical rollover of the high-seas arms embargo authorizations and welcomes the draft's reaffirmation of Libya's sovereignty and territorial integrity. To ensure a balanced approach, we ask the penholder to incorporate language from our May statement on close coordination with Libyan institutions and on capacity-building for relevant Libyan departments. We also believe the Sanctions Committee should take the lead on disposal of seized items in a transparent manner.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as circulated and the six-month extension of the high-seas arms embargo inspection authorizations. We welcome the reaffirmation of Libya's sovereignty and the emphasis on full implementation by all Member States and all Libyan parties. We encourage timely reporting and continued targeted implementation, without adverse impact on the Libyan people.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the authorizations for the strict implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya. We welcome this balanced technical rollover and call on all Member States and Libyan parties to fully implement the embargo and refrain from actions that undermine the political process. We also support continued timely reporting by the Secretary-General on implementation.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation remains unconvinced that the current high seas inspections mechanism has delivered tangible results in preventing arms deliveries to Libya. We would therefore abstain on the text as drafted. To enable us to support it, the draft should include a mandatory effectiveness review and explicit safeguards requiring full respect for international law and UNCLOS, and should ensure the regime does not impede legitimate maritime trade or humanitarian supplies.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the authorizations, but the Council must strengthen the role of the 1970 Committee and ensure transparent reporting on inspections, seizures and disposal. We also ask the penholder to reinforce protection language on migrants and refugees in the light of recent tragedies off Libya's coast. These changes would align the text with A3+ priorities and enable our positive vote.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of the high-seas inspection authorizations and thanks France and Greece for the balanced text. We would like the text to retain an explicit international law and civilian-protection anchor, particularly given recent migrant deaths and clashes, and to make the reporting request more operational on arms embargo violations. These are limited, constructive adjustments; we are ready to work toward swift adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the six-month technical rollover and thanks the penholders. Building on the A3+ position of 29 May, we ask that the text reflect the need for greater transparency and accountability, including reporting on seized items and their disposal, destruction or transfer, and for coordination with the Government of National Unity in implementing the embargo. These additions are important to make the rollover credible from the perspective of the Libyan people while preserving Libya's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as circulated and thanks France and Greece for a balanced text. Renewing the high seas inspection authorizations is essential for strict implementation of the arms embargo and for supporting the Libyan-led political process under resolution 2796. We encourage all Council members to support swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports a clean six-month renewal of the high-seas arms embargo authorizations and strong implementation by all Member States. We ask that PP5 be refocused on combating migrant smuggling and human trafficking rather than broad migration and refugee-protection language. We also want PP3 to reflect the UNSMIL strategic review, core political mission and performance benchmarks, and OP2 to make clear that Member States should disrupt illicit arms transfers and share information through the Panel of Experts.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: sovereignty, external interference and foreign-fighter withdrawal accepted; migration language merged with counter-trafficking and coast guard references.
replies.China: partially accepted: transparency, reporting and disposal safeguards accepted; views of Libyan authorities reflected without conditioning the authorizations.
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: Committee role and capacity-building accepted; coordination language streamlined.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: review, UNCLOS safeguards and expanded reporting added, but authorizations remain for the full six months.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: smuggling, trafficking and accountability language added, while protection language was retained.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves the six-month renewal and core inspection authorizations while incorporating transparency, reporting, humanitarian and international-law safeguards. It accommodates most A3+, Chinese, Russian and US concerns without altering the mandate's duration or scope. France expects broad support, with the Russian Federation likely abstaining.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the revised text. We welcome the incorporation of our key concerns on Libyan sovereignty, non-interference, and the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries. We also take note of the balanced migration language, which links saving lives and human rights with counter-smuggling efforts and Libyan capacity-building in accordance with international law. We will vote in favour.
messages.China: China appreciates the revisions on transparency, disposal and reporting, which address our earlier concerns. To further reflect Libya’s ownership and the views of relevant stakeholders, we ask that the Secretary-General’s report be prepared in consultation with the Libyan authorities and relevant stakeholders, without conditioning the authorizations. With this adjustment, China can support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised draft as it stands. It reflects our priorities: effective implementation of the arms embargo through Operation IRINI, protection of humanitarian assistance and search and rescue, respect for international law and human rights, and robust reporting and review. We would resist any weakening of OP5 or OP6 and encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous requests, particularly the explicit recognition of Operation IRINI and the strengthened language on countering migrant smuggling and human trafficking, including support for Libyan coast guard capacity-building in accordance with international law. We support the current text as balanced and operational, and we encourage all Council members to join consensus for its swift adoption. Greece underscores that full implementation of the arms embargo, respect for Libya’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and preservation of search and rescue and humanitarian space remain essential.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised text. Our earlier concerns regarding full compliance with international law, including the law of the sea, and unimpeded humanitarian assistance and search and rescue have been reflected in the draft. We can join consensus on this text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the current text. We appreciate that the penholder has reflected our key concerns on the Committee’s leading role in the disposal of seized items, capacity-building for Libyan departments, and coordination with Libyan institutions. We call for full implementation of the arms embargo in a balanced manner that respects Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the authorizations and commends France and Greece for a balanced text that reflects sovereignty, international law and humanitarian concerns. To strengthen legal certainty and consistency with the law of the sea and refugee law, we request the two refinements in OP4 and OP5. With those adjustments, Panama can vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current draft as a balanced renewal of the arms embargo authorizations. We welcome the safeguards for legitimate maritime activity, humanitarian deliveries, and the protection of migrants and refugees, as well as the strengthened reporting and review provisions. We encourage the penholder to maintain this text for adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: We appreciate the incorporation of UNCLOS safeguards and expanded reporting. However, the text still prejudges the effectiveness of Operation IRINI and preserves a six-month authorization without a meaningful review; we cannot support it in this form. We ask the penholder to neutralize the IRINI reference and to make the three-month review report-based, with the Council able to modify, suspend or terminate the authorizations in light of its findings.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised text. We welcome the strengthened role of the 1970 Committee in the disposal of seized arms, the enhanced reporting requirements, and the balanced language on maritime inspections, humanitarian access, and protection of migrants and refugees. We encourage all Council members to unite behind this renewal in support of Libya’s political process and the protection of civilians.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the revised draft and supports its adoption. Our earlier concerns on international humanitarian and human rights law, civilian and migrant protection, accountability, and full compliance with international law in implementation and reporting are now reflected. We encourage effective implementation of the arms embargo, transparency in inspection and disposal, and close cooperation with UNSMIL and Operation IRINI, and we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft as presented. Our earlier priorities on enhanced coordination with the Government of National Unity and stronger reporting and accountability for seizures and disposal are reflected in OP2 and OP6. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and to ensure full respect for Libya's sovereignty, territorial integrity and Libyan ownership of the political process.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as it stands and thanks the penholder and co-sponsor for their inclusive engagement. We believe the text strikes the right balance: it renews the high-seas inspections authorizations, reinforces the arms embargo and the call for the withdrawal of foreign fighters and mercenaries, and strengthens reporting, review and transparency. We also welcome its clear emphasis on a Libyan-led political process under resolution 2796 (2025) and on protecting civilians, including migrants and refugees. The United Kingdom is ready to vote in favour.
messages.United States of America: The United States remains ready to support the six-month extension and welcomes the inclusion of UNSMIL core-mission benchmarks, as well as the strengthened focus on smuggling, trafficking and accountability. We still seek to streamline PP5 so it focuses on combating migrant smuggling and human trafficking and holding perpetrators accountable, rather than expansive refugee-protection language. We can support the text with that adjustment.

replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP7 fully reflected; PP9 neutralized but balanced without prejudging effectiveness

We expect broad support with the Russian Federation abstaining, ensuring adoption without a veto.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria indicated support in the last negotiation round and has consistently backed renewals that pair arms-embargo enforcement with sovereignty safeguards, foreign-fighter withdrawal, transparency and humanitarian protections. The draft contains those elements, so Algeria votes in favour.
reasons.China: China had sought changes to ensure Libyan consultation and greater transparency; the penholder accepted the key OP6 request and the draft includes review and disposal safeguards, aligning with China's stated concerns. Therefore China votes in favour while emphasizing sovereignty and effectiveness.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark has consistently supported extending the Libya high-seas arms-embargo authorizations and Operation IRINI, and the draft includes humanitarian, transparency and review provisions consistent with Danish priorities.
reasons.France: France is a co-penholder and consistent supporter of renewing the Libyan arms embargo inspections regime; the draft reflects its priorities and no red lines require abstention or veto.
reasons.Greece: Greece is a co-sponsor and strong supporter of renewing the arms embargo inspection authorizations; the draft aligns with Greece's position and no changes were requested. As co-sponsor, Greece votes in favour and does not need to speak before the vote.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana had expressed support for the draft, made no requests, and has consistently voted in favour of recent renewals of the Libya arms-embargo inspections regime. The text contains safeguards consistent with Guyana’s emphasis on sovereignty, international law, civilian protection, and transparency.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported recent technical extensions and a sovereignty-respecting, transparent implementation of the Libya arms embargo, and the draft incorporates its stated priorities on Committee-led disposal, transparency and capacity-building. With no outstanding requests and prior support in the last negotiation round, a favourable vote is consistent with its record.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports renewing the arms embargo inspections regime and has consistently voted for continuity of Council measures on Libya. Although its OP4 and OP5 requests were only partially reflected, the draft preserves essential safeguards and review mechanisms, so Panama would vote in favour.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported renewals of the Libya arms embargo inspection authorizations, and this draft aligns with its emphasis on international law, humanitarian access and accountability. Voting in favour also reinforces Council support for a Libyan-led political process and transparent implementation.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft neutralizes some Russian concerns but preserves an inspections regime Russia has repeatedly criticized as ineffective and has previously abstained on. Abstention is consistent with its record on extending the Libya high-seas inspections authorization.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported arms-embargo enforcement with stronger Committee oversight and humanitarian/legal safeguards, and those concerns are reflected in the draft; it requested no changes and remains a yes.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported renewals of the Libya arms embargo inspections regime and made no requests for changes in the last negotiation round. It therefore votes in favour while emphasizing international law, humanitarian access and civilian protection.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported the renewal of the Libya arms embargo inspections regime and joined earlier A3+ statements welcoming greater transparency, accountability, and protection for humanitarian and search-and-rescue activities reflected in the draft. With no outstanding requests in the final negotiation round, Somalia would vote in favour without taking the floor before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom has consistently supported renewals and refinements of the Libya arms embargo inspections regime, and this draft matches its stated priorities on implementation, transparency, humanitarian safeguards, and UNSMIL’s political role. With no UK requests outstanding, it would vote in favour and explain support before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a consistent supporter of extending the Libya arms embargo authorizations and secured its requested change to PP5. The draft aligns with US priorities on transparency, accountability, counter-smuggling, and UNSMIL’s core political mission, while not containing the divisive language the US has previously criticized.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the authorizations for the implementation of the arms embargo, which remains essential to preventing the further militarization of Libya and to safeguarding prospects for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. At the same time, we stress that all enforcement measures must be implemented in full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, for international law, including the law of the sea, and for the protection of civilians, migrants and refugees, including the principle of non-refoulement. We welcome the call for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries and the emphasis on transparency in the disposal of seized arms. Implementation must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue, and the reporting and review provisions must be fully honoured. Algeria will continue to support UNSMIL’s core political role and the implementation of the road map in line with resolution 2796 (2025).
before.China: China welcomes the revisions made to the draft, including the strengthened role of the 1970 Committee in the transparent handling and disposal of seized arms and related materiel, the review clause, and the requirement for consultation with the Libyan authorities and relevant stakeholders. China supports the renewal of the authorizations while stressing that all inspections and enforcement measures must be implemented in full respect for international law, the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Libya, and the principle of Libyan ownership. We hope that the effectiveness and transparency of the inspections regime will be genuinely improved and that the Secretary-General’s reporting and the three-month review will provide the Council with a sound basis for further adjustments as necessary. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly support the extension of the authorizations for the implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya. Operation IRINI remains an essential mechanism for disrupting arms flows and supporting accountability, and we welcome the draft’s emphasis on full compliance with international law, including the law of the sea, and its safeguards for humanitarian assistance and search and rescue. We also value the strengthened reporting, transparency and review provisions, as well as the call for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of foreign fighters and mercenaries. We urge all Member States to cooperate fully with IRINI, the Committee and the Panel of Experts, and to uphold their obligations under the arms embargo.
before.France: France will vote in favour. With Greece, we have prepared a balanced and operational text renewing the arms embargo inspection authorizations for six months while strengthening transparency, accountability and review. The Secretary-General’s reporting shows that the arms embargo remains essential: illicit arms transfers, foreign fighters and mercenaries, and trafficking continue to threaten Libya’s sovereignty and the prospects for a Libyan-led political process under the UNSMIL road map. The text also preserves humanitarian assistance and search-and-rescue activities and recalls the obligation to respect international law, including non-refoulement. France calls on all members to support the draft so that the Council speaks with one voice in support of Libya’s unity and stability.
before.Guyana: Guyana will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of the authorized inspections regime because it advances the full and effective implementation of the arms embargo while reaffirming Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity. We welcome the draft’s emphasis on international law, including the law of the sea, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, search and rescue, non-refoulement, transparency in the disposal of seized arms, and a review of the regime’s effectiveness. Guyana continues to support a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations and calls on all Member States and Libyan parties to comply fully with the arms embargo and to cooperate with the Committee and the Panel of Experts.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of the authorizations in a manner consistent with international law, the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya, and the principle that Libya’s future must be determined by the Libyan people through a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We welcome the emphasis on transparency, notification, consultation with the Libyan authorities, the leading role of the 1970 Committee in the disposal of seized arms, and capacity-building for relevant Libyan institutions, as these elements respond to important concerns regarding the effective and accountable implementation of the arms embargo. Pakistan also underscores the need to protect civilians, including migrants and refugees, to respect international humanitarian law and human rights law, and to avoid impeding humanitarian assistance and search and rescue operations at sea. We reiterate our call for full respect for Libya’s sovereignty and for close coordination with the Libyan authorities and relevant stakeholders in the implementation and review of these measures.
before.Panama: Gracias, Señor Presidente. Panamá votará a favor del proyecto de resolución. Apoyamos la prórroga de las autorizaciones para la implementación del embargo de armas, pues su interrupción debilitaría la paz y la seguridad en Libia y la región. Valoramos que se hayan incorporado referencias a la consulta con el Estado del pabellón y las autoridades libias y a la protección de los derechos humanos y el principio de no devolución; sin embargo, seguimos considerando que la función del Comité debe ser de coordinación y no de dirección en la disposición transparente del material incautado, y que las salvaguardias de derecho internacional de los refugiados deben ser plenas y no condicionadas. Estaremos atentos al examen previsto en la resolución.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the authorizations for the implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya. We believe that full and effective implementation of the embargo, in strict accordance with international law, including the law of the sea, is essential to curbing illicit arms flows and creating conditions for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We also stress that inspections and related measures must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue at sea, and must fully respect human rights and applicable refugee law. The Republic of Korea remains concerned by the humanitarian and migration situation in the Mediterranean and calls for accountability for smuggling and trafficking, as well as enhanced regional cooperation and support for Libyan capacity-building. We welcome the provisions on reporting, transparency and review, which will enable the Council to assess the effectiveness of the inspections regime. For these reasons, the Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation appreciates the penholder’s efforts to reflect some of our concerns, including by inserting a review clause and by making the reference to Operation IRINI more balanced. However, our position on the inspections regime remains unchanged in substance: it has not demonstrated the effectiveness that would justify its further automatic extension, and Operation IRINI has still not produced convincing results in preventing illegal arms deliveries. We also believe that any maritime inspections must fully respect international law and the sovereignty of Libya. For these reasons, the Russian Federation will abstain on the draft resolution.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone will vote in favour of this draft. We support the extension of the inspections authorizations because effective implementation of the Libya arms embargo is essential to protect civilians and create conditions for a Libyan-led political process. We welcome that the text strengthens the lead role of the 1970 Committee in the transparent disposal of seized arms, calls for full respect for international law, including the law of the sea and refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement, and ensures that inspections do not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue. We also value the reporting and review provisions, which are important for accountability, effectiveness and respect for Libya’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Sierra Leone urges all Member States and Libyan parties to comply fully and to cooperate with the Committee and Panel of Experts.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of the authorizations for inspections on the high seas off the coast of Libya, which remain an important means of enforcing the arms embargo and preventing illicit arms flows that fuel instability. We stress that all measures must be implemented in full conformity with international law, including the law of the sea, human rights law and, where applicable, refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement, and must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue. We also call for transparency and accountability in the handling of seized materiel, for continued cooperation with Operation IRINI and the Libyan authorities, and for all parties to engage in good faith with the United Nations-facilitated political process and to protect civilians, migrants and refugees.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We thank France and Greece for their work in bringing the Council together on a text that renews the high seas inspections authorisations and places needed emphasis on full implementation of the arms embargo, transparency in the handling of seized materiel, and respect for international law, including humanitarian and refugee law. The United Kingdom remains clear that all Member States and Libyan parties must implement the embargo fully; that external interference and the presence of foreign fighters and mercenaries must end; and that the inspections regime must remain effective, accountable and subject to review. We also stress that these measures must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue at sea, and that the protection of migrants and refugees remains paramount. The United Kingdom continues to support UNSMIL’s mandate and the Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process, including the road map announced by the Special Representative, and we urge all parties to engage seriously towards free, fair, transparent and inclusive elections.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favor of this resolution. We support extending the authorizations for implementation of the Libya arms embargo, and we welcome the strengthened focus on transparency, accountability, and review of the inspections regime. We continue to believe UNSMIL should focus on its core political mission, as set out in the strategic review, and that all efforts should support a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of our views in paragraph 5, including the focus on countering migrant smuggling and human trafficking. We call on all Member States and Libyan parties to fully implement the arms embargo, prevent illicit arms transfers, and ensure that seized materiel is handled transparently. The United States remains committed to Libya’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and stability.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African Members of the Security Council plus (A3+), namely Guyana, Sierra Leone, Somalia and my own country, Algeria.

The A3+ voted in favour of the resolution just adopted renewing the authorizations for the implementation of the arms embargo on the high seas off the coast of Libya. We did so because the full and effective implementation of the arms embargo remains essential to preventing the further militarization of Libya and to preserving the prospects for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process.

The A3+ welcomes the improvements made in the text, including the strengthened role of the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1970 (2011) in the transparent handling and disposal of seized arms and related materiel, the requirement of consultation with the Libyan authorities and relevant stakeholders, and the reporting and review provisions. These elements are important for accountability, transparency and the effectiveness of the inspections regime.

At the same time, we stress that all enforcement measures must be implemented in full respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya and for international law, including the law of the sea. Inspections and related measures must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue operations at sea, and must fully respect the human rights of all persons and applicable international law, including, where applicable, international refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement.

The A3+ also reiterates its call for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries from Libya without further delay. We urge all Member States and all Libyan parties to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel of Experts, to prevent illicit arms transfers, and to refrain from any external interference that could undermine Libya’s peace, stability and political transition.

The A3+ remains committed to a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations Support Mission in Libya, leading to free, fair and transparent national elections and to unified Libyan institutions that reflect the will of the Libyan people. We will continue to follow the implementation of this resolution closely and to support the Libyan people in their efforts to achieve peace, stability and reconciliation.

Thank you.
after.France: Thank you, Mr. President. France welcomes the adoption of this resolution, which renews for six months the authorizations for inspections on the high seas off the coast of Libya. The text is balanced and operational: it strengthens transparency, accountability and review; reaffirms Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity; and ensures that implementation of the arms embargo does not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue and fully respects international law, including non-refoulement. We thank all delegations that supported this text. The arms embargo remains indispensable to curbing illicit arms transfers, the presence of foreign fighters and mercenaries, and trafficking, which continue to threaten Libya’s stability and the prospects for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process under the UNSMIL road map. France will continue to work with its partners, including Greece and Operation IRINI, and calls on all Member States and all Libyan parties to implement the embargo fully and to cooperate with the 1970 Committee and the Panel of Experts. The Council’s broad support today sends a clear message in favour of Libya’s unity, stability and sovereignty.
after.Greece:
Thank you, Mr. President. Greece voted in favour of this resolution. As co-penholder with France, we welcome its adoption by 14 votes in favour. This renewal is not a routine exercise: it preserves the legal framework for inspections on the high seas off the coast of Libya and is an essential tool for giving effect to the arms embargo, preventing illicit arms flows by air, land and sea, and countering the destabilising presence of foreign fighters and mercenaries.

We stress that the authorisations must be implemented in full conformity with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and with full respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Libya. Inspections must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue operations at sea, and all measures must fully respect human rights and, where applicable, refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement.

We welcome the strengthened provisions on transparency, reporting and review, as well as the role of the 1970 Committee in the transparent handling and disposal of seized arms and related materiel, in consultation with flag States and the Libyan authorities. We also support capacity-building for relevant Libyan institutions so that Libya can eventually implement the embargo independently.

For Greece, as a Mediterranean State with maritime borders, the situation off Libya is a direct and serious concern. The recent loss of life in the Mediterranean is a stark reminder of the need to counter migrant smuggling and human trafficking, hold perpetrators accountable, enhance regional cooperation and protect the most vulnerable. Libya’s stability is indispensable for the control of irregular migration and for the security of the wider Mediterranean region.

We call on all Member States and all Libyan parties to implement the arms embargo fully and effectively, to cooperate with the Committee, the Panel of Experts and Operation IRINI, and to engage in good faith with the United Nations-facilitated Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process under resolution 2796 (2025) and the road map announced by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Greece remains committed to a stable, sovereign and united Libya, free from foreign interference, and will continue to support this Council’s active engagement on this agenda item. Thank you.
after.Slovenia: Thank you, Mr. President. Slovenia welcomes the adoption of this resolution. The renewal of the high seas inspections authorization is a concrete contribution to the implementation of the arms embargo and to preventing illicit arms flows that fuel instability in Libya and the wider region. We appreciate the strengthened provisions on transparency, reporting and review, as well as the safeguards for humanitarian assistance, search and rescue, and full respect for international law, including refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement. We call on all Member States and Libyan parties to cooperate fully with the 1970 Committee, the Panel of Experts and Operation IRINI. The broad support demonstrated today should now be translated into renewed support for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process facilitated by UNSMIL, and for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries from Libya. Slovenia remains committed to Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity.
after.Somalia: Thank you, Mr. President. Somalia voted in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the high seas inspection authorizations because the effective implementation of the Libya arms embargo remains essential to preventing further militarization, protecting Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity, and sustaining prospects for a Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. We welcome the strengthened role of the 1970 Committee, the reporting and review provisions, and the call for the complete and verifiable withdrawal of all foreign fighters and mercenaries. At the same time, Somalia stresses that all inspections and enforcement measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including the law of the sea, and must not impede humanitarian assistance or search and rescue. We underscore the need to protect migrants and refugees and to respect the principle of non-refoulement. We also call for greater transparency, accountability and consultation with the Libyan authorities in the handling and disposal of seized arms, and for a serious review of the regime’s effectiveness. Somalia remains committed to working with Council members, including its A3+ partners, in support of a peaceful and stable Libya.
